The closest match is a paper on emotion recognition in conversation that directly studies how much prior context is needed: it finds performance saturates quickly, with about 90% of the gain coming from the most recent 10–30 preceding turns, depending on the label set [1]. It also reports that sentence-level structure helps mainly when no turn-level context is available, but that benefit disappears once conversational history is included [1].

A second paper on multi-turn dialogue shows that much less history can often be enough for language models: using only the most recent user–assistant exchange or compact summaries of prior assistant turns often matches full-context performance, though some cases still need more of the conversation [2]. None of the supplied papers specifically isolates “sentence starters” in the sense of first words or discourse openings for mood detection, beyond the discussion of discourse-marker position in emotion recognition [1].
